note: Recorded ceilings for rules that cannot be decided by a source scan. Each number is a RATCHET: it may fall (and should be tightened in the same commit), never rise. It exists so an unscoped SQL fragment or a missing test suite has to be triaged instead of appearing quietly.

tenantSqlFragmentDetail.excludedReason: `organizations` is the tenant root and `sessions` is resolved by an opaque token hash; neither has an organizationId column to scope by. Every other table in the verified schema is tenant-owned.
tenantSqlFragmentDetail.phase6Tightening: The ceiling was 19 and the count reached 20 when Phase 6 added RoutingRepository, whose `where %s` is filled by scope.predicate("r"). That fragment is genuinely scoped. Rather than raise the ceiling, the scan now recognises an explicit scope marker composed right after the text block (scope.predicate(/ScopedWhere/CrmQueryScope/.formatted(scope) and stops counting it. The count fell 20 -> 3, so the ceiling was tightened to 3 in the same commit. A fragment that stops composing the scope stops being excused.
tenantSqlFragmentDetail.whyItIsNotABoolean: The predicate is frequently appended by CrmQueryScope.select(...) or ScopedWhere rather than written inside the literal, so a text scan sees a fragment with no organizationId in a statement that IS scoped. Example: crm-core CaseRepository.QUESTION_SELECT is completed by scope.select(...). Deciding this soundly needs a call-graph engine (ArchUnit, PMD, or an explicit scope marker); until a backend-owned Gradle module exists, the count is ratcheted and every new fragment is triaged by hand.
